title: Talks on Habit
author: William James
translator: From Talks to Teachers on Psychology (public domain, Project Gutenberg #16287)
blurb: The father of American psychology on why we are 'walking bundles of habits' — and four rules for building better ones.

plastic.e: A child's mind is plastic — it learns languages fast.

habit.m: Something you do regularly, often without thinking.
habit.e: Brushing your teeth before bed is a habit.

habits.m: Something you do regularly, often without thinking.
habits.e: Brushing your teeth before bed is a habit.

resolution.m: A firm decision to do something.
resolution.e: Her New Year resolution was to read daily.

gratuitous.e: A gratuitous cold shower builds willpower.

cards.title: Walking bundles of habits
cards.text: William James's warning to young people: you are setting into habits right now. Every small choice repeated becomes who you are, so pay attention while you are still 'plastic' enough to change.
cards.quote: how soon they will become mere walking bundles of habits
cards.qMean: We quickly become little more than our habits.
cards.qLife: Your morning phone-check routine runs on autopilot before you're even awake.
cards.cap: Neapolitan Woman (1866), by Bernhard Reinhold · public domain

cards.title: Second nature
cards.text: Habit is a second nature — the Duke of Wellington called it ten times nature. By adulthood, our trained habits have replaced most of our natural impulses.
cards.quote: Habit is thus a second nature
cards.qMean: Habits become as natural to us as instinct.
cards.qLife: After years of driving, you change gear without thinking.
cards.cap: Sir Arthur Wellesley, 1st Duke of Wellington · public domain

cards.title: No exceptions
cards.text: James's second rule for a new habit: never allow an exception until it's firmly rooted. One slip is like dropping a ball of string you're winding — it undoes many turns.
cards.quote: Never suffer an exception to occur till the new habit is securely rooted in your life
cards.qMean: Don't skip even once until a new habit is solid.
cards.qLife: Not missing a single morning walk in the first month.

cards.title: Act at once
cards.text: Resolutions don't build habits; actions do. Act on a good intention the very first chance you get, or the feeling fades and leaves you weaker.
cards.quote: Seize the very first possible opportunity to act on every resolution you make
cards.qMean: Act on a good decision immediately, before the feeling fades.
cards.qLife: Signing up for the course the moment you decide, not 'next week'.

cards.title: It's all being counted
cards.text: A character in a play keeps drinking, saying 'I won't count this time!' James replies: you may not count it, but your nerves and brain are counting every time.
cards.quote: We are spinning our own fates, good or evil, and never to be undone.
cards.qMean: Every small choice adds up to the life we end up with.
cards.qLife: 'Just one more episode' every night adds up to months of lost sleep.
cards.cap: Rip Van Winkle and Gnomes · public domain

cards.title: Practise being heroic
cards.text: Do something difficult every day for no reason except that it's difficult. Then, when a real test comes, you'll be ready — like buying insurance.
cards.quote: Keep the faculty of effort alive in you by a little gratuitous exercise every day.
cards.qMean: Do one hard thing daily just to keep your willpower strong.
cards.qLife: Taking the stairs instead of the lift, even when you're tired.
cards.cap: Staircase at Southeast Angle, Painted Chamber, Westminster · public domain
